messages.subject: MG CFA error message: problems with unequal sample sizes?
messages.subject_clean: MG CFA error message: problems with unequal sample sizes?
messages.body_plain:
Hi everyone,

I am trying to run a multi-group CFA with blavaan for the first time.
 The CFA works well but when I add the "group=x" in the command, I
always get the error message [1] "Error in dat$Obsvar[i, (dat$Nobs[i]
 + 1):nvar] <- allvars[!(allvars %in%  : \n  number of items to
replace is not a multiple of replacement length\n". The sample sizes
 of my groups vary from N=77 to N=111. When I only use N=77 for every
group, the model works fine again. Is there a problem with using unequal
 sample sizes in MG CFA in blavaan or am I missing something obvious?

Here is my code:

ObedM1<-'Obed=~Soz8_OB+Soz9_OB+Soz10_OB+Soz11_OB
Soz8_OB ~~ Soz10_OB'

testMG<-bcfa(ObedM1,data=dataobed,group = "country", burnin = 1000, sample = 1000

Thank you so much in advance!

Ronja

Ronja,

Sorry for the delay. I had a look at this and was able to run some simple models with many groups and unequal sample sizes. I am thinking that there might be some missing data issue that is specific to your dataset. I wonder whether your model works in lavaan, something like:

cfa(ObedM1, data=dataobed, group="country")

If not, perhaps the lavaan error message provides a clue.

If so, would it be possible for you to send me your dataset? (off list if needed)

Thanks,
Ed

I can output the mcmc draws from blavInspect, but I would prefer to see the diagnostic plots provided by blavaan.  Any thoughts?

Thank you,

David

messages.subject: Re: Plots for monitored parameters using mcmcextra
messages.subject_clean: Plots for monitored parameters using mcmcextra
messages.body_plain:
It looks like the plot() command in blavaan will not currently allow plotting of things from mcmcextra. But the plots are actually coming from the bayesplot package, and it is not too tough to get those plots after extracting the draws. For your model, you could do something like this:

## extract + arrange draws in the needed way:
draws <- aperm(as.array(blavInspect(fit_horse, 'mcmc')), c(1, 3, 2))

## trace plots:
library(bayesplot)
mcmc_trace(draws, pars = c('lambda_p', 'tau'))

And this page shows you many different plots that are available from bayesplot (the commands usually start with "mcmc_"):

https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/bayesplot/vignettes/plotting-mcmc-draws.html

Ed
